paper.title: From the spin eigenmodes of isolated Neel skyrmions to the magnonic bands of a skyrmionic crystal
paper.figure: Sec. III text: skyrmion radius vs D at constant A = 9.25 pJ/m

Ku1_r1.why: the paper prints 'Ku = 0.65 kJ/m2', which is an areal energy, not an anisotropy. Neither natural reading works: 0.65 MJ/m3 as a bare Ku gives Keff = -3.7 kJ/m3 (no perpendicular easy axis, skyrmion swells to the frame); 0.65 MJ/m3 as Keff gives Ku1 = 1.30 MJ/m3 and the skyrmion collapses below D = 2.5. 788 kJ/m3 (Keff = 134 kJ/m3) was determined from the D = 1.0 target and then reproduced the INDEPENDENT D = 3.0 target to 0.5%.

Ku1_r2.why: same unit problem; 17.2 MJ/m3 is SmCo5's textbook anisotropy, which is why that reading is used. Shape term added back for consistency. The frame is hard enough that this barely matters.

frame_width.why: the paper states a frame surrounds region 1 but not its width

targets.name: diameter at D = 1.0 mJ/m2
targets.source: p.4 text: 'radius increases from about 10 to 25 nm when D is lifted from 1.0 to 3.0 mJ/m2' - read as DIAMETER, since a 25 nm radius does not fit a 38 nm region. USED to determine Ku1_r1.

targets.name: diameter at D = 3.0 mJ/m2
targets.source: same sentence. NOT used for fitting - this is the independent check.
